propositions: Batching N candidates into one call per ordering reduces judge call count from 2N to 2*ceil(N/batch), eliminating repeated prefix copies and reducing input tokens by ~48% against the pre-8415 baseline.

A batch protocol section in the system prompt adds ~436 tokens, lifting the hoisted query digest prefix from 873 tokens to 1,337 tokens, crossing the 1024-token cache floor and enabling prefix caching (write 1,331 then read 1,331).

Batched verdicts must be demultiplexed by label not position; a missing or unknown batch entry abstains only that candidate without affecting others, and a malformed response yields empty results with no exception propagating.

Relation labels shift conservatively on 6/12 ordered pairs when judging with batching (moving mostly away from false flags), with true-positive recovery unaffected by five surrounding negatives, but the shift is systematic not noise.
A shared query digest hoisted into the system prompt must remain unchanged between orderings, with the labelled candidate list placed only in the user message to preserve call-count reduction.
